newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares drift down as Wall Street dips.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares drift down as Wall Street dips.

text.p: Italian shares slipped lower through a subdued trading day on Monday ignoring the turnaround in domestic bonds and the firmer lira, and watching the early dip on Wall Street and the softer trend to other European bourses.

They added that there was little buying interest in early trading with many international investors acting cautiously due to some talk of a need for a further mini-budget early next year, while stocks failed to respond to a rally from early bond weakness and the lira which continued to strengthen.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.35 percent at 10,448 while the Mib30 index was down 0.44 percent at 15,637.

ENI slipped after seeing a new high of 8,090 lire Friday as investors adjusted their portfolios to take into account its full weighting in the Morgan Stanley index (MSCI). Profit-taking set in today and shares ended off 1.29 percent at 7,946 lire.

Olivetti edged ahead early but then ended off 1.6 percent at 530.3 lire after a weekend interview with British Telecom's head of European operations said the group was studying a bid for Omnitel, where Olivetti is the major shareholder.
BT's Pat Gallagher said its alliance with Mediaset and BNL in its Albacom venture was set to expand rapidly, and it would study the prospect of possibly making an offer for the Omnitel.
Mediaset ended off 0.57 percent at 7,208 lire.
Among other major blue chip stocks, Fiat slipped 2.29 percent to 4,356 lire, while Montedison was down 0.65 percent at 1,066 lire and Edison was off 0.45 percent at 9,599 lire.
